We need to fix the CODESYS compilation error: using enum literals incorrectly. In CODESYS ST, enum literals should be qualified with the enum type name, but CASE label cannot use qualified enum? Actually, typical CODESYS supports enum constants in CASE if the CASE selector is the enum type. The error suggests 'ProductionState#IDLE' is not recognized as literal or symbolic integer constant. Maybe syntax for accessing enumeration member in CODESYS is TypeName.Member? But in CASE labels, it may require only the member name? Let's recall: In CODESYS, you define:

TYPE ProductionState : (IDLE, TO_WASH, AT_WASH, ...);
END_TYPE

Then you can assign using ProductionState.IDLE or IDLE (if unambiguous). In CASE with variable of type ProductionState, labels can be IDLE, TO_WASH, etc. directly. The error shows they used ProductionState#IDLE which is not valid. The # syntax is for some other languages, not CODESYS. So fix: replace ProductionState#IDLE with just IDLE, etc. In the CASE state OF ... labels should be enum member names. Also in assignment state := IDLE; etc. (or ProductionState.IDLE). Since we have a local variable state of type ProductionState, direct member names should be recognized as enum constants? Actually, in CODESYS, you cannot use bare enum constants in assignments unless they are unambiguous; they are typically referenced as TypeName.MemberName. But within a CASE on a variable of that enum type, the labels are written as MemberName only (no type prefix). The error shows the labels are not recognized. So change all ProductionState#IDLE to IDLE, ProductionState#TO_WASH to TO_WASH, etc. in both CASE labels and assignments (maybe also states are assigned with type qualification). But assignments also need qualification? In CODESYS, you can do state := ProductionState.IDLE; or state := IDLE; if the compiler understands. Given the CASE error, maybe direct member names are not known? We need to ensure assignment uses valid syntax. Let's check typical CODESYS: For a variable of enum type, you can do var := EnumType.Member; or var := Member;? Actually I think you must use EnumType.Member because the member is not in global scope. But some versions allow it if no conflict. However, the CASE label error says cannot convert ProductionState#IDLE to type PRODUCTIONSTATE. That means they tried to use enum constant in CASE, but the constant expression is not recognized as a symbolic integer constant? Actually the error says "CASE label requires literal or symbolic integer constant". So maybe they need to use integer constants? But enum members are symbolic constants? In CODESYS, enum members are constants of the enum type, which are integer constants? Should be allowed. But the # syntax is wrong; should be '.'? Maybe the correct syntax is ProductionState.IDLE. Let's test: In CODESYS structured text, to refer to an enumeration constant, you use TypeName.EnumValue (dot notation). I believe that's correct. But in CASE labels, you can also use just EnumValue if the selector is of that enum type, because the label is implicitly converted. Let's check typical CODESYS examples:

TYPE STATE : (IDLE, RUNNING, FAULT);
END_TYPE

VAR
    currentState : STATE;
END_VAR

CASE currentState OF
    IDLE:
        ...
    RUNNING:
        ...
END_CASE;

This is valid because currentState is STATE, so labels are expected to be STATE values. In assignments: currentState := IDLE; also valid. I think CODESYS allows using enum members directly if there is no ambiguity, but to be safe we can use STATE.IDLE, and for CASE labels maybe also STATE.IDLE is allowed? But the error indicated CASE label requires literal or symbolic integer constant, so maybe STATE.IDLE is acceptable. I'll change to STATE.IDLE? Actually they wrote ProductionState#IDLE with #, which is not valid. Dot is valid. So use ProductionState.IDLE etc. In both CASE labels and assignments. But note: In CASE labels, you can also use the qualified name? Let's see: "CASE label requires literal or symbolic integer constant". The qualified name STATE.IDLE is a symbolic constant? I think yes. So we can use ProductionState.IDLE in CASE labels as well. To be safe, use qualified names throughout for enumerations and assignments. Since the error specifically points out ProductionState#IDLE as "Unknown type", it's the # that is wrong. So replace # with '.'.

Also check if any other syntax issues: In VAR, we declared local_temp : REAL := 0.0; and used it later. That's fine. In the FUNCTION_BLOCK body, we have an IF Mode THEN ... ELSE ... END_IF. That's fine. But note: In automatic mode, when transitioning from AT_WEIGHT to TO_FIRING, we set state := TO_FIRING but do NOT set MotorForward immediately? Actually the CASE for AT_WEIGHT ends after assigning state := TO_FIRING, and because we are in that CASE, the outputs for MotorForward were set to FALSE at the beginning of the AT_WEIGHT branch. But the next scan will set MotorForward TRUE. The task says "At the same time, the motor starts forward rotation, moving the material to the firing station." That implies motor should start forward in the same scan when weightComplete and qualified. Our current implementation sets state := TO_FIRING but leaves MotorForward FALSE until next scan because the AT_WEIGHT branch sets MotorForward := FALSE and doesn't change it after state change. That is a same-scan transition issue: we should set MotorForward := TRUE immediately when transitioning to TO_FIRING. The public requirement says "At the same time, the motor starts forward rotation". So we need to adjust: after setting state := TO_FIRING, set MotorForward := TRUE. Similarly, when transitioning from AT_WASH to TO_WEIGHT: we set state := TO_WEIGHT and set MotorForward := TRUE already. When transitioning from AT_FIRING to TO_OUTPUT: we set state := TO_OUTPUT and set MotorForward := TRUE already. When transitioning from AT_OUTPUT to IDLE when sensor removed, we set CompletionLight FALSE and state := IDLE; outputs for MotorForward etc already FALSE from AT_OUTPUT branch? Actually AT_OUTPUT branch set MotorForward FALSE, kick FALSE, firingTemp local_temp, CompletionLight TRUE. When sensor removed, we set CompletionLight FALSE and state := IDLE, but firingTemp remains local_temp and MotorForward remains FALSE. That may be okay; firingTemp should maybe be cleared? The spec only says CompletionLight turns off; nothing about firingTemp after completion. It might retain last value. That's okay.

The only same-scan issue is AT_WEIGHT -> TO_FIRING for qualified: need MotorForward := TRUE. Also for unqualified, we set state := REJECTING and kick := TRUE; MotorForward remains FALSE from AT_WEIGHT branch, which is correct because kick is rejection, no motor forward. The spec says "If the material is unqualified, the rejection command kick is initiated." No motor movement; that's fine.

Now, we also need to ensure that in automatic mode, when state changes, we don't leave stale outputs from previous branch? In our CASE, each branch fully sets the outputs for that state before any transition. In transition, we may override some outputs after setting state. That's okay because we are still inside the current branch's execution until END_CASE, so we can set outputs after state assignment. But note: The CASE executes the selected branch based on the state at the start of the scan. If we change state within the branch, the outputs we set after state change will apply to the new state, but the next branch (for new state) will not execute this scan. So we need to manually set the outputs that the new state would have set in its own branch at the same scan. Usually, the new branch's outputs will be applied next scan, but if we require immediate output, we need to override.

We already do that for transitions: TO_WASH -> AT_WASH: we set MotorForward FALSE immediately. AT_WASH -> TO_WEIGHT: we set MotorForward TRUE and state. AT_WEIGHT qualified -> TO_FIRING: we need MotorForward TRUE. AT_WEIGHT unqualified -> REJECTING: we set kick TRUE. TO_FIRING -> AT_FIRING: set MotorForward FALSE. AT_FIRING -> TO_OUTPUT: set MotorForward TRUE. TO_OUTPUT -> AT_OUTPUT: set MotorForward FALSE. AT_OUTPUT -> IDLE: set CompletionLight FALSE; no other outputs need change.

The unqualified transition sets kick TRUE and state REJECTING; the REJECTING branch would also set kick TRUE and MotorForward FALSE, firingTemp 0; but since we set state and kick, firingTemp remains 0 from AT_WEIGHT branch, which is correct because we set firingTemp := 0.0 at beginning of AT_WEIGHT branch, and after qualifying we set firingTemp := local_temp; for unqualified we don't change local_temp (still 0). So after state := REJECTING, firingTemp is 0, kick TRUE, MotorForward FALSE. That's okay.

Thus we must add MotorForward := TRUE after state := TO_FIRING in the qualified case.

Now, about the enum references: Replace all ProductionState# with ProductionState. (dot). For example: state := ProductionState.TO_WASH; and CASE labels: ProductionState.IDLE: etc. In CODESYS, I think qualified names are acceptable in CASE labels. To be safe, maybe use unqualified names in CASE labels? But then assignment still needs qualified. We can use both; for CASE labels, just use the member name because the selector is state: ProductionState, so it knows. That might be simpler and less error-prone. However, the error indicated that they tried using ProductionState#IDLE, which is invalid. So we can either use IDLE, TO_WASH, etc. as labels. For assignments, use ProductionState.IDLE. Let's do that: CASE state OF
    IDLE: ...
    TO_WASH: ...
    ...
END_CASE
And assignments: state := ProductionState.TO_WASH; etc.

Check if there are any other compilation issues: In VAR, local_temp is declared after state, which is okay. But we use local_temp in automatic mode before it's assigned? In the qualified branch we do local_temp := 500.0 + ...; then firingTemp := local_temp; and state := TO_FIRING. Later, in subsequent scans, we use firingTemp := local_temp; that works. But when entering automatic mode from manual, local_temp might have previous value; but we reset it in IDLE branch? In IDLE branch we don't reset local_temp; but we don't use it until qualified weight completes. On qualified weight, we set local_temp, so it's fine. But if unqualified, local_temp remains whatever; but firingTemp is set to 0 anyway. So okay.

Potential issue: In automatic mode, when we are in AT_OUTPUT and sensor removed, we set state := IDLE; but we do not reset local_temp or firingTemp to 0. The spec does not require clearing firingTemp after completion; it may retain last firing temperature. So okay.

Now, we also need to ensure that in manual mode, we don't have any automatic state interference. Since we don't use state in manual mode, it's fine. When switching back to automatic, state might be leftover from previous automatic cycle; but we start in IDLE when Mode becomes true? The spec does not specify reset on mode change, so we assume state persists. But careful: If user switches to manual while in middle of automatic, then back to automatic, state might be in some AT_* state, expecting signals. That could be problematic but unspecified. We can leave as is.

Now check the CONTRACT_RULES JSON: We have none, so output [] is fine.

Now produce repaired code with both required comments. Make sure to keep ENGINEERING_CONTRACT comment as provided but fix enum references and add MotorForward TRUE on qualified transition.

Also, ensure that in automatic mode, when state is TO_WASH and SensorWash is already true from previous scan? Our state machine sees SensorWash true only after entering TO_WASH, which is triggered by SensorFeed. If SensorFeed and SensorWash both true in same scan, we would enter TO_WASH and then in TO_WASH branch we check SensorWash and transition to AT_WASH immediately. That's fine: motor forward would be set TRUE at start of TO_WASH branch, then after seeing SensorWash we set MotorForward FALSE and state AT_WASH. So same-scan transition works. All good.

Now compile: We need to ensure no other errors. The FUNCTION_BLOCK name is ProductionControl, matches task. Inputs/outputs correct.
